meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: to beat, to hit, to strike
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to beat, to hit', paired with 'побить'.

examples.text: Почему меня все бьют в этом доме?
examples.trans: Why does everyone beat me in this house?

examples.text: Тише, Ваня, осторожно! Зачем ты бьёшь дерево ногой?
examples.trans: Easy, Vanya, be careful! Why are you kicking the tree with your foot?

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
At the start of a sentence. Core Russian pron meaning 'everything, all; that's it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: medical practitioner; often used as form of address

examples.trans: Doctor, I urgently need a cast.
It hurts, it hurts! It hurts very much, Doctor!

examples.text: Я умоляю вас, доктор! Это всё ради любви!
examples.trans: I beg you, Doctor! This is all for love!

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
злая собака = vicious dog; а почему вы такая злая? = why are you so hostile?
A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: meжду нами = between us; между прочим = by the way, for your information

examples.trans: For your information, I am the chairman of the court.
You two sort it out between yourselves here.

между.governs: instrumental (or genitive in a few set phrases)

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'всегда').

examples.trans: Say that you are leaving for good.

meanings.note: В награду = as a reward. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'града'). Common feminine noun meaning 'reward, award, prize' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: То есть награды для меня не будет?
examples.trans: So there will be no reward for me, then?

examples.text: Он получил высокую награду за работу.
examples.trans: He received a high award for his work.

examples.text: Никакой награды не будет, Аркадий Борисович!
examples.trans: There will be no reward at all, Arkady Borisovich!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
With не / нет. Core Russian det meaning 'no ... at all, not any' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
Locative / directional adverb. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

плевать.gloss: not to care, couldn't care less (+ dative)

meanings.en: couldn't care less, don't care (colloquial predicative: мне плевать на + accusative)
meanings.note: Lit. to spit. Core Russian adv meaning 'not to care, couldn't care less (+ dative)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Если тебе плевать на дочь, то мне нет!
examples.trans: If you don't care about our daughter, I do!
My parents don't care about me.

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach
meanings.note: К + dative. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.

Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: + dative: 'позвони мне' = call me. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone', paired with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

полениться.gloss: to be too lazy, hesitate to make an effort

meanings.en: to be lazy, spare the effort
meanings.note: не поленился = did not hesitate, took the trouble

examples.text: Чужой человек из Москвы не поленился.
examples.trans: A complete stranger from Moscow took the trouble.
He took the trouble to walk on foot.

meanings.note: Used in the singular. Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

посадить.gloss: to seat; to plant; to put in prison

meanings.en: to put in prison, to lock up
meanings.note: Colloquial. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'садить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to seat; to plant; to put in prison', paired with 'сажать'.

meanings.en: to sit somebody down, to seat
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'садить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to seat; to plant; to put in prison', paired with 'сажать'.

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'садить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to seat; to plant; to put in prison', paired with 'сажать'.

examples.text: Аникеев? Ну что, проворовался? Да я тебя посажу!
examples.trans: Anikeev? Well then, caught stealing? I'll put you in prison!

meanings.note: In потому что. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').
Потому и = that's exactly why. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Кого о чём. Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упредить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to warn, notify in advance', paired with 'предупреждать'.

examples.trans: And they warned me very strictly!

meanings.note: mostly in set phrases: между прочим = by the way, for your information; и прочее = and so on

examples.trans: For your information, I am the chairman of the court.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, здесь же ребёнок, мы завтракаем. А телевизор, между прочим, наш!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, there's a child here, we're having breakfast. And the television, by the way, is ours!

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Plural: дети. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.
Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасать'.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'son' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
'а то' at the start of a sentence: 'а то мы уже начали беспокоиться' = we were starting to worry

examples.text: А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: We were starting to worry, you see.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: В тюрьме = in prison. Common feminine noun meaning 'prison, jail' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In prison it will be much worse.

examples.text: Но я же вижу, как тебе плохо. В тюрьме будет намного хуже, поверь мне.
examples.trans: But I can see how bad things are for you. In prison it will be much worse, believe me.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Уходи! = Go away!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away', paired with 'уйти'.
+ infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things
Чужой человек = a stranger. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('someone else's, foreign').

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
